1.title: Time Intelligence, Statistics, Semi-Additive Measures and Calculation Groups
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Time Intelligence, Statistics, Semi-Additive Measures and Calculation Groups. It covers the exam area Model the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Implement time intelligence measures. Use basic statistical functions. Create semi-additive measures. Create calculation groups. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Model the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Time intelligence measures
1.text: Time intelligence measures. Time intelligence compares and accumulates values over dates: year to date, the same period last year, rolling windows. These functions need a proper date table: one row per day, no gaps, marked as the date table and related to the fact table (see Module five). Always pass the date column of the Date table, never the date column of the fact table.

1.title: Time intelligence measures, continued
1.text: Time intelligence measures. The figure shows this: A year-to-date line and a prior-year line built from one measure and a shifted set of dates.

1.title: Time intelligence measures, continued
1.text: Time intelligence measures. total Y T D. Year-to-date total of an expression; a shortcut for calculate with dates Y T D. dates Y T D, dates Q T D, dates M T D. Return the dates from the start of the year, quarter or month up to the last date in context; used inside calculate. same period last year. Shifts the dates in context back exactly one year. date add. Shifts the dates by any number of days, months, quarters or years; a negative number goes back.

1.title: Time intelligence measures, continued
1.text: Time intelligence measures. dates in period. Returns the dates of a period from a start date; used for rolling windows such as the last three months. parallel period. Shifts the period and returns the whole period, so a partial month becomes a full month. Exam tip: date add shifts the dates you have; parallel period returns the full parallel period. same period last year is the same as date add with minus one year.

1.title: Time intelligence measures, continued
1.text: Time intelligence measures. The pattern for a prior-period comparison is calculate of the measure with a date-shifting function as the filter. Variables keep the year-over-year change readable and make sure each value is calculated once. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Time intelligence needs a contiguous Date table marked as the date table. Use the date column of that table in the function, or the result is wrong or blank.

1.title: Basic statistical functions
1.text: Basic statistical functions. average, min, max. The mean, the smallest and the largest value of a column. median. The middle value of a column. standard deviation sample and variance sample. Standard deviation and variance of a sample; standard deviation population and variance population are for the whole population. percentile inc. The value at a percentile from zero to one, with both ends included; percentile exc leaves them out.

1.title: Basic statistical functions, continued
1.text: Basic statistical functions. count rows. The number of rows of a table in the current filter context. rank X. The rank of each item by an expression; descending by default, so rank one is the highest. top N. A table of the top N rows by an expression, used inside calculate or an iterator.

1.title: Basic statistical functions, continued
1.text: Basic statistical functions. The aggregation functions take a column and ignore blanks. The X versions, such as median X and percentile X.I N C, evaluate an expression for each row of a table first. For rank X, give the table as all of the items, for example all product names. Otherwise the filter context leaves one item in each row, and every item gets rank one. Exam tip: standard deviation sample and variance sample are for a sample; standard deviation population and variance population are for a full population. rank X needs all around the items to rank against all of them, and top N returns a table, not a single number.

1.title: Semi-additive measures
1.text: Semi-additive measures. Not every number can be summed across every dimension. Additive. Rule: Can be added across all dimensions. Example: Sales amount, units sold. Semi-additive. Rule: Can be added across some dimensions but not across time. Example: Account balance, inventory on hand, headcount. Non-additive. Rule: Cannot be added at all; recompute it from its parts. Example: Ratios, percentages.

1.title: Semi-additive measures, continued
1.text: Semi-additive measures. A balance table stores a snapshot per day. If a monthly matrix adds the daily snapshots, the result is far too high. A semi-additive measure uses the last value in the period, and still adds across accounts or products. last date. The last date in the current filter context, even when no data exists on that day. last non blank. The last date that has a value for an expression; it returns the last known balance. closing balance month. The value on the last date of the month in context; versions exist for the quarter and the year. first date, opening balance month. The opening counterparts.

1.title: Semi-additive measures, continued
1.text: Semi-additive measures. The average over time is another valid measure for a snapshot, but it is not the closing balance. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Never sum a balance or an inventory level over time. Use calculate with last date, or last non blank when the last day may have no row, or closing balance month.

1.title: Calculation groups
1.text: Calculation groups. A calculation group is a set of calculation items that change how any measure is calculated. The classic use is time intelligence: one group with the items Current, Year to date and Prior year works for every measure, so you write three items instead of three variants of each measure.

1.title: Calculation groups, continued
1.text: Calculation groups. Create. In Model view, choose Calculation group (or use T M D L). Prerequisite. Discourage implicit measures must be turned on; Power B I Desktop asks to change it. Calculation item. A dacks expression that uses selected measure, the measure being evaluated. Applies to. Explicit measures only, never implicit ones. Precedence. Set in the Properties pane; it decides the order when two groups affect one measure. Dynamic format string. A format expression on an item, so a year-over-year item shows a percentage while the others show currency. Benefit. Fewer measures: twenty measures and three items replace sixty measures.

2.title: Calculation groups, continued
2.text: Calculation groups. A calculation item for year to date wraps selected measure in calculate with dates Y T D. To limit an item to some measures, test with is selected measure. The group appears in the model as a column that you place on a matrix column area or in a slicer. Exam tip: Calculation items use selected measure, work only on explicit measures, and need Discourage implicit measures turned on. Use precedence when two calculation groups combine, and a dynamic format string to change the format per item.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A matrix must show year-to-date sales by month. The model has a Date table that is marked as the date table. Which function should the measure use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: total Y T D over the date column of the Date table. total Y T D accumulates the measure from the start of the year, and the other options either shift the period or use the fact table's date column.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An Inventory table stores Units On Hand once per product per day. A monthly matrix adds the daily values and shows numbers that are far too high. The matrix should show the closing quantity of each month. What should you use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: calculate with the sum of Units On Hand and last date of the Date column. A semi-additive measure takes the value on the last date of the period instead of adding values over time.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A balance measure uses last date and returns blank for months whose last day has no row in the table. Which change returns the last known balance of each month? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Replace last date with last non blank over the Date column. last non blank returns the last date that actually has data, whereas last date returns the last date in context even when it is empty.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A model has twenty measures. Analysts want a year-to-date, a prior-year and a year-over-year version of each. What is the most efficient way? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Create one calculation group with three items. One calculation group with three items that use selected measure applies to all explicit measures without duplicating them.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An author starts to create a calculation group in Model view, and Power B I Desktop asks to change a model setting. Which setting is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Turn on Discourage implicit measures in the model. Calculation groups work only with explicit measures, so Discourage implicit measures must be on.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A table lists products with their sales. Each row must show the product's rank among all products, with the highest sales ranked first. Which function should the measure use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: rank X over all of the products, using the sales measure. rank X returns a rank for each item, and all keeps every product in the ranking instead of only the current row.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which function shifts dates by any number of intervals? Answer: date add. Question two. Which function returns the last date that has data? Answer: last non blank. Question three. Which function inside a calculation item returns the measure being evaluated? Answer: selected measure.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which function gives the standard deviation of a sample? Answer: standard deviation sample. Question five. Which function returns the top N rows of a table by an expression? Answer: top N. Question six. What must a Date table be for time intelligence to work? Answer: Unique, contiguous dates, marked as the date table.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Requirement: Contiguous Date table marked as the date table; pass its date column. Year to date: total Y T D, or calculate with dates Y T D. Prior period: same period last year, date add (any interval), parallel period (full period). Rolling window: dates in period from a start date and a negative number of intervals. Statistics: median, standard deviation sample and variance sample for a sample, percentile inc, rank X with all, top N returns a table. Semi-additive: Balances and inventory are not summed over time; last date, last non blank, closing balance month. Calculation group: Model view; selected measure; explicit measures only; Discourage implicit measures; precedence. Format: A dynamic format string changes the format per calculation item.
